reason: The sources provide 18 multi-cited claims about the star's discovery, properties, and extreme energy output.
story: Hidden 25,000 light-years away behind thick cosmic dust sits the Pistol Star, a blue hypergiant that breaks the scales of stellar physics. Discovered by astronomer Don Figer using the Hubble Space Telescope in the early 1990s, this monster is at least 1.6 million times more luminous than our Sun. It is so radiant that it pumps out as much energy in just 20 seconds as the Sun produces in an entire year. Without the dust, it would be a 4th-magnitude star visible to the naked eye. But the Pistol Star is unstable. It has already blasted away ten solar masses in giant eruptions, creating the pistol-shaped nebula that gives it its name. Its stellar winds are 10 billion times stronger than the Sun’s. Within three million years, this giant will end its short, violent life in a supernova or hypernova explosion. This behemoth reminds us that in space, the biggest giants live fast and die young.
angle: The Pistol Star radiates as much energy in just 20 seconds as the Sun produces in an entire year.

claims.claim: The Pistol Star is a blue hypergiant and Luminous Blue Variable star.
It is located approximately 25,000 light-years from Earth.
The star is located in the Quintuplet Cluster near the Galactic Center.
It was discovered by astronomer Don Figer using the Hubble Space Telescope.
It produces as much energy in 20 seconds as the Sun does in one year.
The star is estimated to be 1.6 to 1.7 million times more luminous than the Sun.
Its radius is estimated to be over 300 times that of the Sun.
If placed in our Solar System, its surface would extend past the orbit of Mars.
The star ejected roughly 10 solar masses of material in giant outbursts 4,000 to 6,000 years ago.
Its stellar wind is over 10 billion times stronger than the Sun's.
Interstellar dust near the Galactic Center absorbs almost all its visible light.
Without dust, it would be a 4th-magnitude star visible to the naked eye.
It is expected to end in a supernova or hypernova in 1 to 3 million years.
The star is named after the pistol-shaped nebula it illuminates.
Its initial mass is estimated to have been as high as 200 solar masses.
The surrounding Pistol Nebula contains shells of gas spanning about 4 light-years.
The star's effective surface temperature is approximately 11,800 to 12,000 Kelvin.
It is located in the southern constellation Sagittarius.

disputed: Current mass estimates vary significantly between 27.5 and 150 solar masses; the script should note mass is uncertain.
Luminosity was once estimated at 10 million solar luminosities but is now generally cited around 1.6 million; the script should treat the higher number as an earlier finding.
The exact discovery year is cited as the 'early 1990s' by some and 1997 by others; the script should refer to the early 90s for the initial identification.
Variability as an LBV is considered 'candidate' or 'not confirmed' by some sources; the script should attribute this as its scientific classification.
